name: Delaware
dueDateNotes: Heads up: while the schedule below uses the federal dates, Delaware's own first-quarter estimated payment is due April 30 (not April 15). The remaining Delaware due dates (June 15, September 15, and January 15) match the federal ones.
selfEmploymentNotes: Delaware applies graduated rates (2.2% to 6.6%) to your federal AGI after a modest standard deduction ($3,250 single / $6,500 married) and a $110-per-person personal credit that is subtracted from your calculated tax. Single and married filers use the same brackets. Self-employed Delawareans also owe the state's gross receipts tax on business revenue, and those working in Wilmington owe an additional city wage/earned-income tax of about 1.25% that this calculator does not include.
uniqueFacts: Delaware levies a gross receipts tax on the total revenue of a business, in addition to income tax; self-employed people can owe it on their gross 1099 income.
Delaware gives a $110-per-exemption personal credit that is subtracted from your tax, not your income.
Wilmington imposes its own earned-income (wage) tax of roughly 1.25% on residents and people who work in the city, on top of the state income tax.
